results.question: What is the maximum I can contribute to a traditional IRA for 2024 if I'm 40?
results.answer: For 2024, if you are 40, the maximum you can contribute to a traditional IRA is $7,000. If you contribute less than the limit, you generally can’t contribute more after the due date of your return for that year to make up the difference.

citations.quote: For 2024, you can contribute to a traditional IRA up to: • $7,000, or • $8,000 if you were age 50 or older by the end of 2024.
If contributions to your traditional IRA for a year were less than the limit, you can’t contribute more after the due date of your return for that year to make up the difference.

results.question: For 2025, what is the IRA contribution limit for someone age 55?

results.question: If I reach age 72 after December 31, 2022, at what age do I have to start required minimum distributions from my traditional IRA?

results.question: What additional tax generally applies to IRA distributions taken before age 59 1/2?

results.question: How often can I do an IRA-to-IRA rollover?
results.answer: You can make only one IRA-to-IRA rollover in any 1-year period (regardless of how many IRAs you own), aggregating all of your IRAs for the limit.

citations.quote: You can make only one rollover from an IRA to another (or the same) IRA in any 1-year period regardless of the number of IRAs you own.

results.question: For an IRA owner who died, by when must distributions generally be completed for beneficiaries who aren't eligible designated beneficiaries?
results.answer: For beneficiaries who aren’t eligible designated beneficiaries, the IRA must be fully distributed by the 10th anniversary of the owner’s death under the 10-year rule (i.e., by December 31 of the year containing the 10th anniversary of the owner’s death).
